title: Cohomological smoothness
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, and $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$
with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, as in the
global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. In the purity
conventions [def-pur-conventions], fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite
extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, its
valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer
$n\geq1$. Put $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$; thus $\ell$
is invertible on the schemes in sight. Work on the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the derived
pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],
[def-weil-derived-tensor], the category $D^b_{ctf}$ of bounded constructible
complexes of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the
compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
and its constructible exceptional right adjoint $Rf^!$
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of
finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with separatedness
defined in [def-weil-proper-morphism] and finite type in
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put
$\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$, where $\Lambda_Y$ is the constant coefficient
sheaf in degree zero. Write $\varepsilon_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to\operatorname{id}$
for the adjunction counit.

The morphism $f$ is *cohomologically smooth* if all three conditions hold:

1. The object $\omega_f$ is tensor-invertible: there exists
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ with
$\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M\cong\Lambda_X$ and
$M\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X$.
2. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the specified canonical map
$$
\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f\longrightarrow Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint transpose under $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$
of the composite
$$
\begin{aligned}
Rf_!(Lf^*K\otimes^L\omega_f)
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!(\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*K)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{f,\omega_f,K}^{-1}}
Rf_!\omega_f\otimes^LK\\
&\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}\otimes\operatorname{id}}
\Lambda_Y\otimes^LK\xrightarrow{\sim}K.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here the first arrow is tensor symmetry; $\operatorname{PF}$ is the
transformation [def-exchange-projection], whose invertibility on this
domain is [fix-prop-projection-formula].
3. For every compact-support Cartesian square [def-cbc-compact-support-square]
(and hence [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]) in this setting, with $g$
arbitrary,
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y,
\end{array}
$$
the specified canonical map
$$
\beta_{f,g}:Lg'^*\omega_f\longrightarrow\omega_{f'}=Rf'^!\Lambda_{Y'}
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint transpose under
$Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ of
$$
Rf'_!Lg'^*\omega_f
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!(\omega_f)^{-1}}
Lg^*Rf_!\omega_f
\xrightarrow{Lg^*\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}}
Lg^*\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{Y'}.
$$
The exchange map in this composite is the transported pro-etale map of
[def-cbc-exchange-map]. The constructible exceptional functor above is
transported from the etale one, so $\omega_f$ has an etale-origin witness
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness];
[thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] says that the exchange map is an
isomorphism and is unchanged under replacing that witness by an
isomorphic one.

No smoothness or dimension is assumed in this definition, and no
identification $\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ is part of it.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
a separated finite-type
morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *cohomologically smooth* if:

1. $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ is tensor-invertible;
1. for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the canonical map
(the mate of the projection formula of
[def-exchange-projection] with the adjunction counit)
$$
\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f
\longrightarrow Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism;
1. for every Cartesian square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\ g'\ }&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ g\ }&Y,
\end{array}
$$
the canonical base-change map
$Lg'^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ is an isomorphism.
